segmentation: The segmentation map outlines the camera wearer's lower torso, legs, and arms at the top of all five frames (3–5 m away, facing backward/upward away from the trailer tongue), as well as the second person moving away on the upper right in frames 4 and 5 (3–5 m away, positioned to the right of the toolbox and reaching left into the compartment out of arm's reach of the wearer). Across the sequence, the wearer's segmented right arm shifts backward to lift the triangular lid in frame 2 and reaches into the open compartment in frames 3–5, while the second person's arm and bent legs recede toward the top-right edge in frames 4–5 to grasp the same strap. While the masks help isolate the overlapping limbs of the two people at the top and right edges from the dark pavement, the map is heavily unreliable for object recognition and boundaries. It misclassifies the trailer bed and tongue as an 'airplane' in frame 1, labels the triangular metal toolbox as an 'umbrella' in frame 2, and mislabels the open toolbox lid and internal chains/straps as 'person' masks in frames 3 and 5. Furthermore, it completely fails to segment the trailer, hitch, and toolbox in frame 4, leaving the entire non-person scene black.
pose: The pose map renders only magenta 3D hand skeletons in the first three frames and contains no yellow body skeletons across any of the five frames because both people's heads and full bodies are largely out of the upward-looking field of view. In frame 1, it detects the camera wearer's left hand resting on the trailer frame (about 3–5 m away, top left), and in frames 2 and 3 it tracks both the wearer's right hand (centre-right, 3–5 m away) and left hand (centre-left, 3–5 m away, separated by ~3–5 m) as they grasp the toolbox latch and prop open the lid out of reach. This skeletal rendering makes the exact finger articulation and pinch grip of the wearer's hands in frames 1–3 easier to read than in the high-contrast RGB image, especially where the right hand in frame 2 is over dark metal. However, the pose map is completely unreliable in frames 4 and 5, where it outputs an entirely black image and fails to detect any hands or bodies despite the camera wearer's hands and the receding second person's right arm and legs being clearly visible and interacting with the strap at 3–5 m distance.
